Whole-body overview, not a drug pathway measured in this structure. These processes can overlap; routes and organs differ between medicines.
For many oral medicines, material crosses the gut lining into blood.
Blood flow, binding and tissue barriers affect where a compound reaches.
Liver enzymes transform many compounds; other tissues also contribute.
Kidneys remove some compounds and metabolites; elimination also has other routes.
A generic single-compartment model starting at 100%, with constant first-order elimination. No absorption, repeat doses, active metabolites or patient variation are modeled.
Remaining fraction = 100% × 2^(−time / half-life). A percentage is not a therapeutic or safe concentration; never use this curve to choose a dose or dosing interval.

Researchers study DNA damage, telomere changes and epigenetic regulation.
Protein quality control and cellular recycling help maintain the contents of cells.
Nutrient sensing and mitochondrial function are connected areas of aging research.
Studies investigate senescence, stem-cell maintenance, communication, inflammation and microbial communities.
This is a research framework, not a validated personal score. Cell or animal experiments do not by themselves establish human benefit, safety or an anti-aging treatment.
